evals.prompt: /plancollab 给 CLI 添加 --verbose 参数
evals.expected_output: Baseline check, Claude generates a plan, invokes Codex CLI for review with consensus update, saves plan.md on approval
expectations: Checks for .plancollab/baseline.md and asks user whether to use existing or rescan (or scan if none)
Skill displays a session header showing task, planner, and reviewer roles
Claude generates a plan containing all 6 sections: Summary, Affected Files, Steps, Design Decisions, Risks, Testing
Other agent is invoked via CLI (codex exec or claude -p)
Communication payload includes contents of .plancollab/baseline.md
Full plan saved to {SESSION}/plans/round-1-cc.md (or -cx if Codex planned)
Full review saved to {SESSION}/reviews/round-1-cx.md (or -cc if Claude reviewed)
Consensus update saved to {SESSION}/reviews/round-1-consensus-cx.md (or -cc) listing agreed and disputed sections
state.json is created with agreed/disputed arrays
Review verdict (APPROVED or NEEDS_REVISION) is displayed to user
If APPROVED, final plan is saved to .plancollab/{session-name}/plan.md

evals.prompt: /plancollab 让 codex 做计划，实现用户认证模块
evals.expected_output: Codex is used as planner (generates baseline + plan via CLI), Claude acts as reviewer directly in conversation
expectations: Planner is set to codex based on user intent
Reviewer is set to claude
If no baseline exists, Codex scans the project via CLI and generates .plancollab/baseline.md
Other agent is invoked to generate the plan, output written to {SESSION}/temp/plan.md
Claude reviews the plan directly in conversation without invoking Codex CLI
Claude produces a consensus update: which sections are agreed, which are disputed
Review includes verdict, strengths, issues table with severity levels, and suggestions

evals.prompt: /plancollab refactor the session management module to support multiple providers
evals.expected_output: Multi-round discussion using consensus-based projection: agreed sections locked as one-liners, disputed sections sent in full
expectations: Round 1: full plan sent to reviewer, consensus update identifies agreed/disputed sections
Round 2 communication payload: agreed sections as one-line references, disputed sections as full text
Codex reviewer sees discussion log so it can track whether prior issues were addressed
Round 2 plan preserves agreed sections unchanged
Each round produces: plans/round-N-{cc|cx}.md, reviews/round-N-{cc|cx}.md, reviews/round-N-consensus-{cc|cx}.md
state.json updated after every round with agreed/disputed lists and rounds array
Communication payload shrinks as more sections reach agreement

evals.expected_output: Scans .plancollab/ for session directories and displays collaboration status including agreed/disputed sections
expectations: Scans .plancollab/ for directories containing state.json
If no sessions found, displays 'no active collaboration' message
If found, displays session list table (task, status, rounds, roles, updated) or single session details

evals.prompt: /plancollab implement a complex caching layer with Redis and in-memory fallback
evals.expected_output: When max rounds reached without agreement, conflict points are summarized with both positions and file references, plus already-agreed sections listed
expectations: After max rounds with no APPROVED verdict, unresolved disagreements are summarized
Each conflict point shows both planner's and reviewer's positions
Conflict summary references specific round files (e.g., {SESSION}/reviews/round-2-cx.md)
Already agreed sections are listed separately
User is asked to decide on each conflict point rather than generic accept/continue/abandon

evals.prompt: /plancollab add WebSocket support for real-time updates
evals.expected_output: First-time use triggers project baseline scan, baseline is saved and reused
expectations: No .plancollab/baseline.md exists initially
Skill asks user for permission to scan the project
Planner scans the project and generates baseline.md with: Project Overview, Tech Stack, Directory Structure, Core Modules, Architecture Patterns, Key Types, Build & Run
baseline.md is saved to .plancollab/baseline.md with a date header
Baseline content is used as project context in the Round 1 communication payload

evals.prompt: Help me redesign the adapter layer to support a plugin architecture
evals.expected_output: Claude generates a non-trivial plan, auto-review triggers, asks user about auto-review preference on first use, then proceeds with Codex review
expectations: Claude generates a plan with multiple files and architectural decisions (non-trivial)
Skill auto-invokes after plan generation (not triggered by /plancollab)
No .plancollab/config.json exists, so user is asked about auto-review preference
If user says 'yes always', config.json is written with auto_review: true
If user says 'no', config.json is written with auto_review: false and review is skipped
If user says 'just this once', review proceeds without writing config.json
On subsequent plans, config.json is read and auto-review behavior follows the saved preference
